description: Reusable visual grammar patterns for Executor-authored PPT SVG. These are design moves, not fixed templates.

grammars.name: 认知重构
grammars.skeleton: past view -> current change -> new judgment
grammars.dominant_object: three-stage reframe cards with the new paradigm visually strongest
grammars.accent_strategy: highlight the changed judgment and the new term
grammars.secondary_content_policy: weaken historical examples and make the new judgment dominant
failure_modes: equal weight between old and new

grammars.name: 阶段跃迁
grammars.skeleton: stage axis + current stage emphasis + outcome cue
grammars.dominant_object: horizontal stage rail with the target stage emphasized
grammars.accent_strategy: use accent color only on the current or desired stage
grammars.secondary_content_policy: compress stage evidence into short captions

grammars.name: 能力放大器
grammars.skeleton: core actor -> amplifier -> expanded capability field
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the amplifier, not every capability point
grammars.secondary_content_policy: turn capabilities into compact labels around the center

grammars.name: 人机分工
grammars.skeleton: human decision blocks + AI execution blocks + final responsibility
grammars.dominant_object: responsibility split with human side visually authoritative
grammars.accent_strategy: accent human responsibility and final judgment
grammars.secondary_content_policy: keep AI tasks as supporting chips

grammars.name: 问题标签
grammars.skeleton: few sharp labels + evidence bullets + bottom quote/takeaway
grammars.secondary_content_policy: move explanation into muted evidence lines

grammars.name: 输入处理输出
grammars.skeleton: input column -> process engine -> output column
grammars.accent_strategy: accent output artifacts and the transformation engine
grammars.secondary_content_policy: keep input items quiet and compact
failure_modes: process looks like a passive list

grammars.name: 焦虑到行动
grammars.skeleton: pressure source -> honest feeling -> concrete action
grammars.dominant_object: central quote or action choice card
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the action sentence, not the anxiety source
grammars.secondary_content_policy: make anxiety sources gray and action options strong

grammars.name: 误区到真实
grammars.skeleton: muted myth list -> directional bridge -> strong reality card
grammars.accent_strategy: accent corrected judgment and mandatory human action

grammars.name: 工作流链路
grammars.skeleton: step chain + phase bracket + artifact tray
grammars.dominant_object: execution chain with a visible output artifact zone
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the handoff from interaction to execution

grammars.name: 四象限案例
grammars.skeleton: 2x2 case map + active case highlight + representative output strip
grammars.dominant_object: active quadrant with numbered case signal
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the first or current case and dim the rest
grammars.secondary_content_policy: compress each case to tags and representative outputs
failure_modes: too much prose in each card

grammars.name: 演示转场
grammars.skeleton: demo path + expectation reset + next action
grammars.accent_strategy: accent what the demo is not and what it proves
grammars.secondary_content_policy: make operational steps compact on the side

grammars.name: 证据型主视觉
grammars.skeleton: problem context -> central evidence artifact -> validation value
grammars.dominant_object: large prototype, demo console, product screen, or screenshot-style proof artifact
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the artifact state and the value proven by it
grammars.secondary_content_policy: keep pain points and value bullets as side evidence around the artifact

grammars.name: 能力成熟度阶梯
grammars.skeleton: lower capability layer -> middle management layer -> upper quality/control layer
grammars.dominant_object: stacked ladder or rising lane that makes capability elevation visible
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the target maturity level and the upward movement
grammars.secondary_content_policy: turn examples in each layer into compact chips

grammars.name: 能力公式引擎
grammars.skeleton: capability equation strip + central engine + component explanation
grammars.dominant_object: capability equation or engine hub that explains how parts become reusable ability
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the resulting capability and the equals/engine transformation
grammars.secondary_content_policy: keep components as short labeled modules with one-line definitions

grammars.name: 流程责任复合
grammars.skeleton: top workflow chain + responsibility split + final owner statement
grammars.dominant_object: workflow chain with visibly attached AI/human responsibility zones
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the handoff and the final human responsibility
grammars.secondary_content_policy: compress per-step details into small labels and reserve room for ownership zones
failure_modes: workflow and responsibility split are disconnected

grammars.name: 案例诊断
grammars.skeleton: case process -> apparent success -> exposed defects -> root-cause takeaway
grammars.dominant_object: contrast diagnosis that makes the root cause stronger than the process timeline
grammars.accent_strategy: keep process and surface results quiet; accent exposed defects and the root-cause conclusion
grammars.secondary_content_policy: compress the attempt process into a narrow lane and reserve the largest area for diagnosis
failure_modes: surface success and defects have equal weight
root cause is buried in a footer

grammars.name: 工程鸿沟桥
grammars.skeleton: demo shore -> engineering bridge/barriers -> production shore
grammars.dominant_object: bridge or gap structure with named engineering barriers as load-bearing elements
grammars.accent_strategy: accent the engineering bridge and production-entry threshold, not the demo endpoint
grammars.secondary_content_policy: keep endpoint descriptions short and use the center for architecture, standards, testing, security, release, and maintenance barriers
failure_modes: page becomes an ordinary step flow
demo and production endpoints look equally complete
engineering barriers are decorative labels without structural weight
